new_entities.name: Acupuncture during IVF
new_entities.description: Acupuncture delivered during ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval, or embryo transfer as an adjunct to in vitro fertilization.

new_entities.name: Live birth rate
new_entities.description: The proportion of treatment cycles or participants resulting in a live birth.

edges.effect_quant: A 2008 meta-analysis of 13 trials and 2,500 women found no significant increase in live birth with acupuncture around embryo transfer (RR 1.34, 95% CI 0.85-2.11), and a 2018 randomized trial found no significant live-birth difference between acupuncture and sham control (84/415 vs 72/409; RR 1.15, 95% CI 0.87-1.52).
edges.population: women undergoing in vitro fertilization or intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles with acupuncture used as an adjunctive therapy
edges.mechanism: Acupuncture may influence stress, autonomic tone, or peri-transfer experience, but any effect on implantation and live birth appears inconsistent and highly sensitive to protocol and comparator choice.
edges.summary: This is a mixed and still disputed adjunctive-care edge. IVF acupuncture may help some intermediate or subgroup outcomes in certain studies, but the strongest sham-controlled live-birth evidence does not support a reliable overall live-birth benefit.
edges.caveats: Do not market this as a proven fertility booster. Apparent gains in some uncontrolled or subgroup analyses do not erase the null result in the large sham-controlled live-birth trial.

evidence.notes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of acupuncture in in vitro fertilisation.
Effect of Acupuncture vs Sham Acupuncture on Live Births Among Women Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

evidence.citation: Smith CA et al 2018 Reprod Biomed Online
evidence.notes: Acupuncture and in vitro fertilisation research: current and future directions.
